title: Sequence-length-tiered SLO engine and decision visualizer
creator: Alex Kim
description: Build a sequence-length–aware SLO derivation engine and an interactive visualizer that helps SREs and product teams tune circuit breaker thresholds and load-shedding policies by sequence-length cohort. This ticket delivers: (1) an offline SLI aggregation pipeline that bucketing requests by requested/observed sequence length, (2) a decision layer that proposes adaptive circuit thresholds per region and per length cohort, and (3) a Grafana dashboard + simulation panel that visualizes expected impact of different policies under synthetic replay traffic.
acceptance_criteria: SLI pipeline emits p50/p95/p99 latency and error-rate metrics segmented by sequence length buckets (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024) and region
Decision engine produces candidate circuit thresholds (latency and error) per region/cohort and exposes them via a config endpoint and a staging API
Grafana visualizer includes: contour heatmap of latency vs traffic by cohort, simulated failover overlay, and policy impact preview for shed/cooldown parameters
Synthetic replay harness can run historical traces and produce expected regional failover and admission rates for a given policy
Docs (Confluence) with runbook steps for SREs to roll out cohorted thresholds using canary and rollback policies
progress: 2025-02-16: Spike completed comparing bucketing strategies (per-request requested_length vs observed_token_count). Decided to use observed_token_count for SLO bucketing to reflect model decode path stress.
2025-02-20: Implemented initial ETL to aggregate token-latency histograms per sequence-length bucket in the metrics pipeline. Prototype uses sample-rate 1/100 to control cardinality.
2025-02-28: Decision engine v0 built as a Jupyter notebook (quantile-smoothing + hysteresis). Notebook linked and used to generate candidate thresholds for eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
2025-03-05: Grafana panels scaffolded; contour heatmap implemented as series heatmap. Basic policy preview UI integrated with the staging config endpoint.

2025-03-10: Ran first synthetic replay across 48h production trace slice. Observed that >1024 cohort causes disproportionate p99 spikes during tail events—added proposal to increase admission backpressure for that cohort by 30% during peak windows.
decisions: Bucket boundaries chosen: 0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024. Rationale: maps to common prompt+generation lengths and avoids overfitting to outliers.
Use observed_token_count for bucketing to include both prompt and decode cost; requested_length was noisy due to streaming edits.
Sampling: initial aggregation uses 1% sample plus deterministic high-priority sampling for enterprise customers to preserve signal for low-volume tenants.
Hysteresis: candidate thresholds include cool-down windows (5m/15m/1h) to avoid flip-flopping during microbursts.
Policy rollout: staged via console canary -> region rollout -> global; visualize impact in dashboard before applying.
Fallback behavior: when a region is unhealthy for a cohort, traffic will be rerouted to compatible model variants with priority-preserving admission scoring.
implementation_notes: Metrics: added labels sequence_bucket and cohort_hash to per-token latency histogram. Avoided high-cardinality labels by limiting buckets and hashing tenant ID to cohort buckets for privacy and cardinality control.
Pipeline: using existing ingestion (prometheus remote write -> clickhouse) with a new hourly aggregator job that computes quantile sketches per region/cohort.
Decision engine: lightweight service (python) that loads sketches and runs threshold optimizer. Exposes /v1/policy/candidates (read-only) and /v1/policy/apply (admin-only with audit logging).
Dashboard: Grafana dashboard mirrors include: sequence_slo_contour, cohort_policy_preview, replay_simulator_panel. Links below.
Testing: unit tests for bucketing, e2e replay test harness for policy simulation against recorded traces.
Ops: added audit events to platform event stream for every applied threshold change to simplify post-mortem analysis.
risks: Cardinality explosion if we later increase bucket granularity — mitigated by fixed buckets and sampling
Decision engine miscalibration could cause over-aggressive shedding for enterprise tenants — gated by canary and tenant-priority preserves
Cross-region traffic spike during failover could overload fallback regions if cohort admission not tuned — mitigated by conservative initial thresholds and simulation
Synthetic replays may not cover new model behaviors (e.g., longer generations) — plan to continuously feed latest traces and add model-version dimension later
